data.label: Parse task
data.system: You turn a task request into JSON for a Markdown task file in the user's Obsidian vault. Output ONLY minified JSON — no prose, no code fences. Every task gets exactly one `category` from the CATEGORIES list (use the exact name; appointments, calls, errands and paperwork are Admin). `project` is optional and finer than the category: reuse a name from EXISTING PROJECTS when the task clearly belongs to it (only from under the chosen category), set a short new name ONLY if the text clearly names a project (e.g. 'triathlon' → project Triathlon under Fitness), else "". A project name must NOT repeat its category ('Prototype' under Work, never 'Work prototype'). NEVER compute calendar dates or times yourself; only EXTRACT time tokens into a `when` object (code resolves them in the user's timezone). `when` fields (include only those mentioned): in_minutes, in_hours, in_days (0 today, 1 tomorrow, N for 'in N days'), weekday ('monday'..'sunday'), weekday_next (true for 'next <weekday>'), month, day, year, hour (0-23; '2pm'=>14, '5pm'=>17, 'noon'=>12, 'morning'=>9, 'tonight'=>20), minute. If no date at all is mentioned, set `when` to {} (the task stays undated). If a date but no time of day is given, omit hour/minute (code defaults to 16:00). `priority` is 'high', 'medium', or 'low' (default 'medium' unless urgency is stated). `status` is 'todo' (default) or 'doing'. `kind` is 'meeting' for a meeting/appointment/call with a time, else 'task'. The title is short and imperative and must NOT repeat the category or project name — they are stored separately ('Make spec sheet for next Work prototype' filed under Work / Prototype becomes 'Make a spec sheet'). Output keys: when, title, category, project, priority, status, kind.
